primitives.name: Cross-Sport Correlation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The first sports betting product where you can run your own hypothesis tests on cross-sport historical data.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_{AB}^{\\tau}(E)': 'Dimensionless cross-sport correlation coefficient', 'X': 'Indicator function for trigger event E in sport A', 'Y': 'Binary outcome (e.g., over/under settled above/below)', '\\tau': 'Observation window (same night, next day, etc.)', '\\mu_Y': 'Marginal mean of Y across all observations', '\\sigma_Y': 'Standard deviation of Y'}
primitives.assumptions: Independent and identically distributed historical game pairs, binary outcomes, sufficient sample size for stable estimates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Small sample sizes (n < 30) lead to unreliable estimates; requires manual warning flags.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Bayesian updating framework for refining historical priors using current trigger events.
layer2.telemetry: Number of historical trigger-event observations per query.

primitives.name: Sharp Money Signal
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Trigger event** — what defines an "event" in sport A.
primitives.latex: S_A(t) = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if sharp money threshold exceeded at time } t \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_A(t)': 'Binary indicator for sharp money in sport A at time t', 't': 'Time variable (game start, halftime, etc.)', 'threshold': 'User-defined volume or delta threshold'}
primitives.assumptions: Market liquidity sufficient to detect significant bets, no front-running by sportsbooks.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Flat betting patterns yield no informative signal; requires minimum betting activity variance.

layer2.mapping: Dual to GSE's state-transition logic for detecting high-conviction trading states.
layer2.telemetry: Volume change percentage relative to baseline for each sport.

primitives.name: Observation Window
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Observation window** — what time horizon to look at sport B.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'W(\\tau)': 'Time interval for observing sport B outcomes', 't_0': 'Start time (trigger event time)', '\\tau': "Duration of observation window (e.g., 'same night' = ~24 hours)"}
primitives.assumptions: Independence between trigger event timing and outcome distribution within the window.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overlapping windows introduce autocorrelation; windows must be disjoint or properly lagged.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's rolling-window state monitoring for sequential decision-making.
layer2.telemetry: Distribution of observed outcomes within each defined window bin.

primitives.name: Confidence Interval
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Confidence interval — never a single percentage without the range.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'CI': 'Confidence interval width for binary outcome probability', '\\hat{p}': 'Observed proportion of positive outcomes', 'z_{\\alpha/2}': 'Critical value from standard normal distribution (e.g., 1.96 for 95% CI)', 'n': 'Sample size of trigger events'}
primitives.assumptions: Binomial sampling distribution, large enough n for normal approximation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: n < 30 requires exact binomial methods instead of asymptotic intervals.

layer2.mapping: Analogous to GSI's credible intervals used for posterior uncertainty quantification.
layer2.telemetry: Width of confidence intervals as a function of sample depth.

It operates on a joint discrete-time stochastic process (X_t, Y_t), where X_t captures structured anomalies (like sharp money) in one sport and Y_t tracks outcomes in another. The key challenge is accounting for异oscedasticity and non-stationarity across different sports and time periods. By providing confidence intervals and sample-count warnings, the engine mitigates overfitting and false discovery while enabling users to construct novel composite strategies.
